Late in a pleasant middle, a noisy queue arose while the kennel attendant was handling it. Companion Animal Travel Desk Incident Report

The situation began with a mixed line of travelers seeking animal check-in support, and the crowd grew restless when one carrier was set aside for review. Voices rose, several travelers pressed forward, and the kennel attendant had to pause normal intake so the welfare coordinator could check the animal's condition and the documentation at hand. <<FACT F120>> The senior coordinator then moved to the counter, separated the waiting travelers into orderly groups, and explained the service sequence in calm, direct terms.

One traveler became upset over the delay and insisted on immediate boarding, while another asked for a change in route handling for a small pet in an approved carrier. Staff confirmed the desk ledger entries, rechecked labels, and kept the animal area clear to reduce stress on the pets already waiting. <<FACT F109>> No animal showed signs of injury, and the carriers remained secure throughout the interruption.

I directed one clerk to continue intake for low-risk cases, another to monitor the queue, and the kennel attendant to stand by for any welfare concern. The senior coordinator approved the temporary hold on the disputed case and reminded staff to record each service change in the desk ledger before release. After the line settled, the travelers were processed in order, the atmosphere returned to normal, and the remaining departures continued without further incident. Follow-up will include a brief review with the desk team and a check of the handling procedure so the same congestion is less likely to recur.
